problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\sqrt{6}{x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{30}} \\ -\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}}\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066805/assets/1ba0b151abea3c5b1a050c6ff924f3718fcb045b063b1b47df7a73f9d15316c9.png) where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing the components of $\mathbf{x},$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-2-6=-8 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-4+3=-1\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $15{x}_{1},$ where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-4)\cdot (-3)}{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2+12}{1+9} \\  & =\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
15{x}_{1}=15\cdot \frac{7}{5}=21.
$$
